bottleneck: Which failed 42 -> 43 extension patterns in R(5,5) recur across diverse frontier parents strongly enough to form a transfer-safe canonical obstruction atlas?
associations: orbit-quotiented failure-pattern mining over failed 42 -> 43 extensions
minimal UNSAT-core style extraction for monochromatic K5-forcing witnesses
canonical subgraph hashing for obstruction reuse across parent families
leave-one-group-out validation where parent families play the role of domains
witness-preserving regression tests for every pruning object
certificate-carrying core reuse between lower-bound pruning and upper-bound lemma generation
rare-tail audits for failures not covered by the dominant obstruction cores

forced_bridges.mechanism: canonicalize the local K5-forcing witness neighborhoods and count orbit-stable motif reuse across failed extensions
treat each failed extension as a forcing certificate and shrink it to a minimal monochromatic K5-generating core
treat parent families as domains and require the obstruction dictionary to survive held-out-family evaluation
use known 42- and 43-vertex witnesses as a non-regression suite for every proposed pruning rule
promote only those canonical cores whose identity survives symmetry changes and can be attached to checker-friendly proof stubs

anomaly_results.result: If the atlas loses nearly all coverage when the most Exoo-like family is held out, the claimed structure is a lineage memorizer rather than a reusable Ramsey object.
A stable core library must canonicalize to the same identities across both high-automorphism and low-automorphism parent families.
If the top cores miss a long tail of failures, the next useful split is not another search heuristic but a second-layer clustering of uncovered failures by local signature.
A filter bank that covers many failures but kills even one known 42- or 43-vertex witness should be retired regardless of coverage gains.
If a recurring core compresses lower-bound failure explanations but cannot survive proof-format replay, it should stay an H1 atlas object and not be sold as H3 reuse.

steering_directions.rationale: This is the novelty-safe center of H1 because it keeps the claim on reusable structure rather than on a better extension engine.
steering_directions.first_step: Materialize frontier_parent, extension_case, and failure_witness records for the first Exoo/Ge/Lehavi packet and measure top-25 core coverage.
steering_directions.expected_signal: At least 30 percent of failed orbit-distinct extensions are covered across at least 3 non-isomorphic parent families.

steering_directions.rationale: Without stable canonical hashes, recurrence can be inflated by symmetry representatives or encoding noise.
steering_directions.first_step: Define the canonical core encoding and test compression before and after canonicalization on the first atlas pass.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Core count drops by at least 2x while witness coverage and core identities stay unchanged under symmetry changes.

steering_directions.rationale: Transfer is the clearest discriminator between a structural Ramsey object and an overfit family-specific catalog.
steering_directions.first_step: Hold out the most non-Exoo-like parent family, rebuild the atlas on the remaining families, and measure held-out coverage retention.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Held-out coverage remains at or above half of the training-side coverage with zero witness-safety violations.

steering_directions.rationale: H1 becomes unusable as soon as its pruning rules delete a known witness, so witness safety has to mature in parallel with transfer.
steering_directions.first_step: Build the witness-survival matrix with rows = known 42/43 witnesses and columns = candidate core-derived filters.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Zero false deletions on the saved witness set plus a measurable reduction in failure cases on the same rung.

steering_directions.rationale: If the dominant cores underperform, the next move is to cluster the uncovered failures rather than opening H2 prematurely.
steering_directions.first_step: Cluster uncovered failures by local signature after the first atlas pass and inspect whether one second-layer family dominates the tail.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Either a small second family appears or H1 is killed quickly for lack of reusable recurrence.

validation_checks.check: Schema completeness and family coverage audit over frontier_parent, extension_case, and failure_witness records.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Every required field is populated from a local artifact or a reproducible import step, and the first packet spans at least 3 parent families.

validation_checks.check: Canonical hash stability under automorphism representatives and encoding permutations.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Equivalent failure witnesses collapse to one canonical core id with no witness-coverage loss.

validation_checks.check: Held-out-family recurrence table and coverage-retention calculation.
validation_checks.pass_signal: At least half of the training-side coverage survives on the held-out family.

validation_checks.check: Witness-survival matrix plus on/off ablation of each filter on the same rung.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Zero witness kills and a measurable failure-case reduction relative to the no-filter baseline.

validation_checks.check: Cluster the uncovered tail and test whether one secondary signature family dominates it.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Either a small new family is isolated for a second-layer atlas pass or H1 is demoted promptly.
